en.title: Table manners
en.summary: Polite behaviour at meals and how to give and follow instructions.

paragraphs: Good table manners put others at ease. This lesson explains the main rules in English-speaking countries and teaches the negative imperative and the time clause with until.

In Britain the knife is held in the right hand and the fork in the left, and the fork is not changed over. In the United States people usually cut the food, then put the knife down and eat with the fork in the right hand. Everyone waits until all have been served before starting. A parent reminds a child before dinner.

lines.speaker: Mum
lines.text: Sit up straight and put your napkin on your lap.

lines.speaker: Mum
lines.text: Wait until everyone has been served. And please don't talk with your mouth full.

lines.speaker: Child
lines.text: May I leave the table when I've finished?

lines.speaker: Mum
lines.text: Yes, if you ask politely. Say Please may I be excused?

lines.speaker: Mum
lines.text: Of course, and take your plate to the kitchen.

lines.speaker: Child
lines.text: Can I have some pudding first?

paragraphs: **1. Negative imperatives forbid.** Use do not (don't) with the base verb; add please to be polite. See Introduction to Grammar: Moods, command, subjunctive and conditional.

blocks.html:
FormExample
Don't + verbDon't talk with your mouth full.
Please don't + verbPlease don't interrupt.
Never + imperativeNever start before the host.
Do + verbDo sit down.

paragraphs: **2. Until introduces the end of a period.** After until, the present simple is used for a future meaning. See Introduction to Grammar: Prepositions and conjunctions.

blocks.html:
FormExample
until + present simpleWait until everyone has been served.
until + nounWait until the end.
beforeWash your hands before you eat.
afterSay thank you after the meal.

items: A napkin protects your clothes; a serviette is another British word for it.
Please may I be excused? asks permission to leave the table.
Elbows on the table and talking with food in the mouth are widely considered rude.
Say Excuse me if you must leave the table.

paragraphs: Manners vary by family and region, but the main ideas are respect and consideration for others. Guests praise the food, wait for the host to begin and thank the cook at the end.
